correctness.rationale: The six-point metric feasibility is precisely two types of triangle inequalities. Cyclic averaging applies to arbitrary scalar linear extensions; the equilateral ℓ_1 zero-sum transport identity gives K≥2L/S and K≥1. Scalarization proves this even for arbitrary Banach-space operator coefficients. In the Pompeiu/three-support phase, weights 1-2r_i/S are probabilities; all source-target norms equal 2L/S and target-target norms are bounded by the pairwise radial spread ≤s. When r_max>sum of the other radii, the two-support kernel has all six-point pair ratios ≤1 by metric feasibility, while 2L/S≤1. At equality the constructions agree. The planar application follows from a 60-degree rotation proof of the Pompeiu inequalities. All 384 rational metrics and 34560 scalar extreme-pair checks passed; five unrestricted LP spotchecks agreed. No inference from finite samples is used for the general theorem.

originality.rationale: A complete sharp simultaneous extension theorem for all feasible circulant three-by-three metrics is not implied by general doubling extensions, one-point Banach extension results, existing matched/nonmatched two-value cross-distances, or geometric three-focus-distance envelopes. The new comparison is the no-penalty result for three coupled target sites with three independent cross distances. Literature evidence and accessible historical statements were compared for stronger implications, not just titles; residual risk of an equivalent unindexed transport kernel remains.

value.rationale: Complete and nontrivial sharp extension classification across all feasible five-parameter two-equilateral-layer cyclic metrics, with arbitrary three distinct cross radii. The coupling cost from three new data sites provably vanishes, including the boundary where the positive optimizer loses a support vertex; the result is independent of the metric parameter s despite the simultaneous target constraints. The Euclidean geometric specialization supplies an exact sharp three-focus boundary between strict amplification and norm-one extension for entire 120-degree point orbits, not only a one-point or fixed-midpoint configuration. This identifies a natural structural phenomenon in finite metric and Banach Lipschitz extension theory; it is not merely a computed small case.
